# zheev

> Computes all eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex Hermitian.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zheev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zheev';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zheev( order, jobz, uplo, N, A, LDA, w, strideW, WORK, RWORK ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' 0 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` 0 `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | `w` stride length |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, 2 * N - 1 )` |  | workspace (length >= `max( 1, 2*N-1 )`, the reference's minimum; `(NB+1)*N`, with NB from `ilaenv`, is optimal); if `null`, a workspace of optimal size is allocated |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, 3 * N - 2 )` |  | real workspace (length >= `max( 1, 3*N-2 )`, the reference's declared extent); if `null`, one of that length is allocated |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A. On exit, if `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, A contains the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then on exit the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zheev.ndarray(
    jobz, uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input/output Hermitian matrix; on exit contains eigenvectors if jobz=`'compute-vectors'` |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A (complex elements) |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for eigenvalues (length N), in ascending order |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for w |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, 2 * N - 1 )` |  | complex workspace array (length from `offsetWork` at least `max(1,2*N-1)`, the reference's minimum, when `N > 0`; `(NB+1)*N`, with `NB` the ZHETRD block size from `ilaenv`, is optimal) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, 3 * N - 2 )` |  | real workspace array (length from `offsetRWork` at least `max(1,3*N-2)`, the reference's declared extent, when `N > 0`) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A. On exit, if `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, A contains the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then on exit the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if zsteqr/dsterf did not converge

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK and RWORK must be sufficiently large

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0` or `N === 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the algorithm failed to converge; i off-diagonal elements of an intermediate tridiagonal form did not converge to zero.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zheev()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHEEV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zheev.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zheev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zheev';

// Eigen-decomposition of a 3x3 Hermitian matrix A (column-major):
const N = 3;
let A = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, -2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 6.0, 0.0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
const w = new Float64Array( N );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 64 * N );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( ( 3 * N ) - 2 );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = zheev( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'upper', N, A, N, w, 1, WORK, RWORK );
console.log( 'info:', info, 'eigenvalues:', w );

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, -2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 6.0, 0.0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
info = zheev.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'upper', N, A, 1, N, 0, w, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'info:', info, 'eigenvalues:', w );
```

</section>
